I am old man, 84 years, and I have farmed this land my whole life here in Iringa. My maize plot is small, less than one hectare, but my family helps me work it together with beans planted between the maize rows. I cannot afford the chemical fertilizer this season — the price is too high and I have no voucher — so I will spread the manure from my few cattle on the plot like my father taught me. I will use the seeds I saved from last harvest, and I depend on the masika rains as God provides; my body is too weak now to do all the work, so my sons and grandchildren will help, and during weeding time I will pay a few neighbors to assist.
